risks.title: Loss of key licenses
risks.score_rationale: This risk factor is central in the 10-K, mentioned among the first risks, with strong language (materially affect, major adverse effect). The share of licensed product sales has declined (43% in 2026 vs 53.4% in 2024), increasing vulnerability. The Industrial category is heavily weighted here as it touches the core of the business model.

risks.title: Dependence on major customers
risks.score_rationale: Presented early in the document, with precise data: 67.6% of sales come from the top 10 customers. The language is alarming (materially adverse effect, loss of a major customer). The trend of increasing concentration in retail purchasing amplifies this risk. The Competition category is critical as it exposes the company to market share losses.

risks.title: Retail strategy failure
risks.score_rationale: Operational losses in retail are documented ($5M in 2026 vs $30.5M in 2024), showing improvement but a still fragile situation. The language indicates a clear risk of failure in the turnaround strategy. The risk is repeated and detailed, highlighting its importance. High weighting for Industrial.

risks.title: Digital cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly tied to information systems, security breaches, and cyberattacks. The language is concerning (problems could reduce sales, increase costs). Digital is a strategic priority, increasing exposure. The Cybersecurity category is moderately weighted but critical here.

risks.title: Reputation and influencers
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned multiple times, particularly regarding social media and influencers. The language is strong (harm to our reputation, regardless of accuracy). The rise of social networks increases exposure. The Reputation category is moderately weighted but rising in importance. Stable context vs N-1.

risks.title: Dependence on CEO Morris Goldfarb
risks.score_rationale: The CEO is explicitly named, with alarming language (materially adverse effect, stock price). The risk is repeated and emphasized as critical. The Key Person category is situational but highly critical here. No clear succession plan is evident.

risks.title: Declining traffic in outlets
risks.score_rationale: The risk relates to store locations and declining foot traffic, with external factors (economy, travel). The language is concerning but less intense than other risks. Mentioned within the retail context, which is decreasing in weight (losses declining). Moderate weighting.

ai_positioning.summary: G-III has not mentioned artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing. There is no indication of AI use or integration in its operations.
